candidates.label: Apollonia (Macedonia, on the Via Egnatia)
candidates.support: A town in Mygdonia, Macedonia, on the Via Egnatia between Amphipolis and Thessalonica, about 30 Roman miles from Amphipolis and 38 from Thessalonica. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site, near the modern village of Nea Apollonia; the International Standard Bible Encyclopedia reports that its name seems to survive in the modern Pollina.

summary.text: Apollonia was a town in Mygdonia, a district of Macedonia, lying a little south of Lake Bolbe on the Via Egnatia, a day's journey between Amphipolis and Thessalonica. Acts records that Paul and Silas passed through Apollonia on their way from Philippi to Thessalonica, without any indication that they stayed there.

history.text: The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia dates Apollonia's founding to about 432 BC, noting that coins attest its existence by the fourth century BC, and reports that its name seems to have survived into modern times as Pollina.
